title: Hooked
novel:
Ted dated a woman named Tiffany who kept him "[[on the hook|on the hook]]." She called only when she needed something, then [[vanished|vanish]] again. Ted waited by the phone like a [[faithful|faithful]] dog.

"She's [[stringing|string]] you along," Barney said. "Cut the [[line|line]]."

But Ted could not. Every smile from Tiffany felt like a [[promise|promise]], even when it led nowhere.

The gang shared their own [[hook|hook]] stories. Marshall had once loved a [[lamp|lamp]] more than reason. Robin had waited years for a man who never called.

Lily, the most [[sensible|sensible]] of them all, sat Ted down. "You [[deserve|deserve]] someone who calls back," she said. "Not someone who keeps you in a jar."

The words [[struck|strike]] him. That night Ted stopped waiting. He deleted Tiffany's number and walked out into the cold air, feeling [[lighter|light]] than he had in months. Some [[obsessions|obsession]], he realized, only held you because you [[refused|refuse]] to let them go.

on the hook.en: kept waiting by someone who will not commit

string.en: to keep someone hoping for something you won't give

line.en: a long thin piece used to catch fish

promise.en: a sign that something good will happen

hook.en: a curved piece of metal that catches things

strike.en: to have a strong effect on someone

obsession.en: something you cannot stop thinking about

refuse.en: to say you will not do something
